Your report shows that your LDL Cholesterol result is 172 mg/dL. It

is flagged as HIGH because this number is above the range printed on your report, which is ‹100. 

LDL stands
for low-density lipoprotein. It carries cholesterol through your blood to your body's cells. It is often called "bad"
cholesterol because when there is more of it than your body needs, the extra can build up in the walls of your blood vessels.
Over many years, higher levels of LDL are linked to plaque building up in your arteries, which raises the risk of heart disease and stroke.
Your doctor can help review this result with you.
